correctness.rationale: A one-dimensional graph vertex has a dominated descending link exactly for a unique earlier neighbor. The first two encountered parts generate every strong matching, and extension of a two-part ordering realizes every component. The exact U_y/V_x cover follows by ordering the first cross-part pair. Its flaps and central simplices have a uniform elementary free-face collapse schedule, with relative intersections two isolated vertices; the graph has 2ab vertices and 4ab-a-b edges and hence first cycle rank 2ab-a-b+1. Singleton edge cases are separate. Global integral homology and full automorphism modules follow from disjoint union and natural Mayer–Vietoris cycle boundary; no torsion. Two scripts independently compare exact faces/Betti numbers for ten cases and verify every free-face collapse. Computations only support finite instances; the general theorem is proved by the combinatorial argument.

value.rationale: A complete, natural unbounded classification of the newly studied strong matching complex for all complete multipartite graphs, with a surprising disconnection law for connected input graphs, an explicit elementary collapse to one-dimensional topology, sharp singleton transitions and global integral symmetry representations. These structural results are neither a mere parameter substitution nor a single finite enumeration. The bipartite component formula alone is not presented as new.
